extracted.intended_audience: poets, creative writers, and literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for poets and writers on achieving and recognising poetic 'simplicity' and the distinction between 'simple' and 'sentimental' poetry; discusses stylistic, moral, and aesthetic qualities that mark genius and good poetic expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of feeling (noble vs foolish)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish childish/foolish simplicity from noble/childlike candor; simplicity of feeling belongs to those 'children in heart' and proceeds from the rectitude of the heart, not from depravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess motive and source of simplicity: is it sincere trust and goodness (worthy of esteem) or mere naiveté that invites ridicule or harm? Example: a good-hearted but inexperienced man who confides his secrets (simple but estimable); counterexample: imprudent candor in a pope (Adrian VI) that may be politically damaging. Evaluate consequences as well as intent when judging simplicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity as a mark of true genius
rubrics_metrics.description: "True genius is of necessity simple, or it is not genius. Simplicity alone gives it this character." Genius is guided by nature and instinct rather than rules or artificial crutches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge genius by whether its utterances and acts spring from instinct/nature and achieve results without reliance on learned artifices. A genius 'issues from the known without ceasing to be at home' and enlarges the circle of nature without overstepping it. Anti-pattern: work that uses elaborate rules or contrivances to simulate depth—this indicates lack of true genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solving complex problems with simplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius solves the most intricate problems 'with simplicity, without pretension, with ease' (e.g., the emblem of Columbus's egg).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate solutions and innovations for whether they simplify complexity elegantly rather than adding complication. The effective criterion is whether the resolution appears natural and inevitable once seen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity in expression and stylistic grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplicity in terms and movement is where grace especially consists; genius expresses sublime thoughts 'with this simple grace' so that the expression and the thought are one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for phrasing where language 'gushes forth spontaneously from the idea' and the sign seems to 'disappear in the thing signified' (originality/inspiration). Anti-patterns include scholastic over-refinement that 'tortures all its words' and enervates thought in an effort to avoid vagueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directness — naming things by their proper name
rubrics_metrics.description: A simplicity of expression consists in naming things by their proper name without circumlocution, in opposition to conventional politeness that forces evasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer direct, unadorned diction that reflects sincere perception (like a child's ordinary expressions). Avoid needless euphemism or convoluted phrasing put in place to observe 'laws of propriety.' This directness is not coarse bluntness but truthful naming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modesty, innocence, and natural character in the person of genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius manifests in private life as modesty, even timidity; it is 'modest, because nature is always so; but it is not decent, because corruption alone is decent'—intelligent but not cunning, faithful to inclination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a creative personality or its work, value signs of modest, non-artful comportment and an absence of affectation. This inward simplicity often parallels the style of their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of artifice and scholastic pedantry
rubrics_metrics.description: The scholastic spirit 'tortures all its words' and uses crutches of feebleness (rules, grammatical pedants) that blunt thought; true poetic expression avoids such artifices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify passages where technique overshadows spontaneity or where restraint has become an affectation; penalize works that prioritize rule-following and verbal gymnastics over natural expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: The poet as guardian of nature — simple vs sentimental poet
rubrics_metrics.description: Two kinds of poetry: the simple poet (poet is nature) and the sentimental poet (poet seeks nature as an idea or object). The simple poet expresses nature directly; the sentimental poet raises nature into an ideal or reflects on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify a poet's work by whether it arises from an inner harmony with nature (simple poetry) or whether it is the product of reflection and idealisation (sentimental poetry). Both are legitimate; evaluate according to consistency and depth of feeling: does the work authentically embody one mode or awkwardly imitate it?

rubrics_metrics.name: Impersonality — poet should hide behind the work
rubrics_metrics.description: The genuinely simple poet 'hides himself behind his work; he is himself his work, and his work is himself,' whereas sentimental/modern poets often interpose their personality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work asks to be read for its own reality rather than as a vehicle for the poet's personality or commentary. Anti-pattern: a poet who intrudes with astonishment or self-conscious aside (Ariosto example) rather than letting the scene speak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of nature vs raising reality to the ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: Ancient poets tended to imitate nature as a living reality; modern poets, living in a civilized/artiﬁcial state, 'raise reality to the ideal' — they represent the ideal rather than the present reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating poetical aims, consider whether the work seeks faithful depiction (mimesis) or idealisation. Both approaches have different merits: faithful depiction attests to a natural unity; idealisation pursues a higher, infinite aim. Judge according to the poet's chosen objective and success at achieving unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic unity — harmony of senses and reason
rubrics_metrics.description: In a natural state the senses and reason act together as a harmonious whole; in civilization they are disunited. Poetry's task varies accordingly: in natural unity the poet imitates reality; in the civilised state the poet must represent the ideal to restore unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate works for their capacity to reconcile feeling and thought—does the poem suggest an integrated humanity (sense + reason) or does it merely dramatize the split? The greater poetic achievement is re-establishing unity appropriate to the poet's condition (imitation in natural mode or idealisation in civilized mode).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity versus epochal/artistic constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple poets are 'scarcely any longer in their place in this artificial age' and may appear as strangers or ill-trained children of nature; critics often dislike rule-breakers even when they embody genius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging originality or simplicity, account for historical/contextual misreading: rule-breaking simplicity may be authentic genius misinterpreted. Do not dismiss works simply because they violate current aesthetic rules; consider whether the simplicity is genuine and productive rather than merely eccentric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentimental poetry characteristics and modern sensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentimental poetry arises when the poetic faculty acts through ideas and reflection; it addresses nature as idea/object and is characteristic of modern/cultivated epochs (examples: Horace, French sentimental poetry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize sentimental poetry by its reflective tone, its orientation toward the ideal or the emotion stirred by nature rather than direct embodiment. Evaluate for depth of reflection and whether sentiment enriches rather than replaces true feeling.
